pr_title: Make `AnsiRegex` able to capture Hyperlink ansi sequences
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #16420
Make `AnsiRegex` able to capture Hyperlink ansi sequences.

With this fix, the repro `dir | ft @{n="link";e={$PSStyle.FormatHyperlink($_.name, ("some random text as a link" + "x" * (random -Max 5) ) )}}, lastwritetime` get the following output

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/127450/170375041-862567d1-eaf6-4bd1-8859-ad78e38daf00.png)

issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] Write a descriptive title.
- [X] Make sure you are able to repro it on the [latest released version](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)

- [X] Refer to the [FAQ](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md).
- [X] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

Format-Table is able to understand that escape sequences don't print when sizing text (otherwise nothing would align) but it has a blind spot when the sequence is for a URL 

`dir  | ft @{n="link";e={$PSStyle.FormatHyperlink($_.name, ("some random text as a link" + "x" * (random -Max 5) ) )}},  lastwritetime` 
Will demonstrate it 

### Expected behavior

```console
link                            LastWriteTime
----                            -------------
6Print                          13/11/2019 10:06:51
archive-vsteam                  13/09/2020 10:57:30
azure-devops-auth-samples       13/11/2019 17:48:16
blog                            25/08/2021 16:45:12
Exiftool                        01/07/2018 11:07:43
```


### Actual behavior

```console
link                                                                        LastWriteTime
----                                                                        -------------
6Print                            13/11/2019 10:06:51
archive-vsteam                    13/09/2020 10:57:30
azure-devops-auth-samples          13/11/2019 17:48:16
blog                            25/08/2021 16:45:12
Exiftool                            01/07/2018 11:07:43
```
```

review_comments: Can we make this more specific instead of using `.*?` which accepts any characters up to an escape?

A hyperlink sequence looks like this: ``"`e]8;;link-url-string`e\link-description-string`e]8;;`e\"``.

Good catch. This regex will remove the whole `link-url-string` which could contain arbitrary characters, such as `//`, `#`, or any other comment indicators in other languages.

I thought about doing validation on the `link-url-string` part and only treat it as hyperlink sequence if the `link-url-string` part is valid http/https urls. But that doesn't work because valid url can have `#` in it, which is the comment indicator for any scripting languages.

I think we need to fix `Out-File` to not change anything if the piped in object is text. It should do the VT sequence striping only when it has to go through the formatting system -- meaning only strip the VT sequences that are added during formatting.

Opened issue https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/issues/17452, and also here is the PR to fix `Out-File` and `Out-String`: https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/17455. The proposed behavior for `Out-File` and `Out-String` is "Leave ANSI out of object formatting, but leave strings alone".
@SteveL-MSFT, @daxian-dbw  Has this issue been resolved satisfactorily?  If so, please resolve and approve.
Yes, I think this is resolved
